title: How to Prepare a Press Release That Journalists Will Read
h1: How to prepare a press release that journalists will read
description: What makes news worth a press release, the facts a writer needs, structure, quotes, media assets, timing, distribution choices and realistic expectations.
intro: A press release can earn media coverage, but only if it carries real news and reaches the right journalists. Many releases fail because the story is not newsworthy, the key facts are buried or they are sent to lists of people who never cover the topic. Freelance writers and PR specialists can help with each step, but you need to bring the story and the facts. This article explains how to prepare and what to expect.

faq.a: Something new and relevant to a publication's readers, such as a launch, research findings, a major partnership or a notable milestone.

faq.q: Does a press release guarantee coverage?
faq.a: No. Journalists decide what to cover. Strong stories and targeted outreach improve the odds.

faq.q: How long should a press release be?
faq.a: Often 400 to 600 words, with the key facts in the first paragraph.

faq.q: Are paid distribution services worth it?
faq.a: They can help with visibility online, but personal outreach to relevant journalists usually matters more.
